title: Adding Elements and Intermediate Array Techniques
summary: Uses the FizzBuzz interview problem to teach push() and pop(), a counter variable, the modulo operator for divisibility, and why the order of if / else if branches matters. Built incrementally as a function that adds one more item to an array on each call.

concepts.heading: The FizzBuzz problem
points: Produce the numbers 1 to 100, but a multiple of 3 becomes "Fizz", a multiple of 5 becomes "Buzz", and a multiple of both (15, 30...) becomes "FizzBuzz".
It is a common screening question because it quickly shows whether a candidate can break a problem into steps.
In this lecture it is built one step at a time: one new item per call of fizzBuzz().

concepts.heading: push() and pop()
points: Arrays can start empty: var output = [];
array.push(value) appends value to the END of the array, never the start or middle. It can be called repeatedly to grow the array.
array.pop() removes the last item from the array (and returns it).
(Extra) shift() and unshift() do the same jobs at the front of the array.

concepts.heading: Counter variable
points: Calling output.push(1) repeatedly would keep adding 1. Instead keep a separate variable count (starting at 1), push count, then increase it with count++ (same as count = count + 1).
Declare output and count outside the function so they persist between calls; if declared inside they would be reset on every call.

concepts.heading: Modulo for divisibility
points: a % b gives the remainder of a divided by b. 12 % 2 is 0 (divides cleanly); 12 % 5 is 2.
count % 3 === 0 therefore means count is a multiple of 3; likewise for 5.
Replace the pushed value with the matching word when the test is true.

concepts.heading: Order of conditions
points: An if / else if / else chain runs the first branch whose condition is true and skips the rest.
If the Fizz test comes first, 15 matches it and Buzz is never examined, so 15 shows as Fizz.
Fix: test the combined case first: if (count % 3 === 0 && count % 5 === 0) push "FizzBuzz"; else if divisible by 3 push "Fizz"; else if divisible by 5 push "Buzz"; else push count.
General rule: put the most specific condition first.

task.name: FizzBuzz one step at a time
task.starting_point: Empty output array and a fizzBuzz function that only logs output.
task.goal: Every call appends the next FizzBuzz item to output and prints the array.
steps: Create count = 1 beside the output array.
In fizzBuzz push count, increment it with count++, then log output.
Add if (count % 3 === 0) to push "Fizz" instead of the number.
Notice 15 gives Fizz only; move the combined (&&) check to the top to produce "FizzBuzz".
Call the function repeatedly (15+ times) and verify the output.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 15 - Intermediate Javascript/15.08 - Adding Elements and Intermediate Array Techniques/script.js

pitfalls: Forgetting count++, so the same number is pushed forever.
Putting the 3 check before the combined 3-and-5 check.
Declaring output or count inside the function so they reset.
Writing = instead of === in the modulo test.
The reference repo's version derives the number from output.length and pops and re-pushes; it works but differs from the counter-based approach in the lecture.

playground.coverage: Covers push, pop, shift, unshift, join and split. FizzBuzz is not part of this lesson (it appears in the 99 bottles/while content).
gaps_and_ideas: Add a FizzBuzz one-call-at-a-time task using count, push and modulo.
Add an order-of-conditions demo showing 15 with the Fizz check first versus last.
Demo idea: a 'Call fizzBuzz()' button that appends to a visible array.
